{{Quote|That's practically a little Empire itself these days - the Garonnin family and the Vandrons and their kind always wanted it to be.|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]|<ref name="Children of the Jedi (novel)">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>}}
The '''Senex sector''' was a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TEA" /> and [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]]<ref name="Western Reaches" /> of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], bordering the [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sector]] and near the [[Ninth Quadrant]], located next to the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]. Though the two [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] were nominally independent of each other, with both the Senex and Juvex sectors returning [[Senator/Legends|senators]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], in practice they were culturally and politically identical, together making up the [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]]. The sector was long independent of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], ruled by an alliance of "[[Ancient Houses]]," including [[House Elegin/Legends|Elegin]], [[House Garonnin|Garonnin]], [[House Taneel|Taneel]], and [[House Vandron|Vandron]] (which was the oldest and noblest).

==History==
{{Quote|The Senex is an autonomous sector, ruled by a line of fiercely self-reliant royal houses. The Republic respects the independence of the Senex worlds, and has no interest in meddling in the affairs of those worlds.|[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Valorum]]|<ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Senex_sector.jpg|thumb|left|205px|The Senex sector and its surrounding [[Sector/Legends|sectors]]]]
The sector was originally settled after the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]], by a group of settlers under the leadership of [[Thull Vandron]]. Vandron and his followers desired to keep central government control to an absolute minimum, and when the Ruusan Reformations failed to meet their standard, they abandoned known space and settled the [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]], where the highest form of government would only be that of the houses controlling individual planets. In [[553 BBY]], a conflict known as the [[Crimson Days]] broke out in the sector, but was ended by the [[Third Nantama Synod]].<ref name="TEA" />

The sector was self-supporting, but desired open trade with the Republic and at the [[Fourth Nantama Synod]], the Houses decided to make peace with the Republic. They tried to establish commercial links with Republic mega-corporations, but the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] stopped this, due to the widespread use of [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] in the Senex sector.<ref name="TEA" /> It gained the right to trade after aiding the Republic in cracking down on the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]], which was based on the Senex planet [[Asmeru/Legends|Asmeru]]. At some point prior to the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the sector was finally permitted into the Republic, and represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by [[Terr Taneel/Legends|Terr Taneel]]. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] maintained only a token presence in the sector, and it never joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. It was the center of the [[Ismaren plot]]. The [[Herzfall Corporation/Legends|Herzfall Communications Corporation]] was based in the sector.

In addition to Asmeru, planets in the sector include [[Hutlar]], [[Karfeddion/Legends|Karfeddion]], [[Neelanon/Legends|Neelanon]], [[Yetoom Na Uun]], [[Mussubir Three]], and [[Senex/Legends|Senex]] itself.

==Behind the scenes==
[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] seems to imply [[Picutorion/Legends|Picutorion]] is in Senex sector, but ''[[The Hunt Within: Valance's Tale]]'' places it in [[Kwymar sector/Legends|Kwymar sector]].
